correctness.rationale: For each order-n de Bruijn cycle the two preceding states as share suffix s and have distinct successors s0,s1, yielding the unique bijective feedback b=a xor f(s). For factors asb, reversal bs^R a occurs if and only if f(s)=f(s^R). Each nonpalindromic suffix reversal pair with equal values contributes two merged factor pairs; each palindromic suffix with f=1 contributes one; each palindromic suffix with f=0 contributes two distinct palindromic factors. Thus the number of reversal classes at length n+1 equals two to the power n, minus twice A, minus P-Z, where P counts palindromic length-(n-1) suffixes. At order five this simplifies to 28-2A+Z. The Python verifier exhausts all 65536 truth tables and independently counts cyclic reversal classes; 2048 full-length feedback orbits have exactly the specified five joint bins. The independent graph-traversal C++ enumerator visits each root-anchored Hamiltonian 32-state cycle once and produces exactly the same five-bin counts, without using feedback invariant equality. Both source files were executed from the package working paths. The full finite calculation proves the order-five spectrum; no higher-order histogram is asserted.

value.rationale: Every binary order-five de Bruijn cycle has the same full factor language through length five, so reflection complexity at length six is the first natural nonconstant statistic of this form. This is a full census of all 2048 cycles with exact forbidden gaps and a general feedback-reversal structural explanation; it discriminates cycles in a motivated earliest-possible way, not a routine arbitrarily selected slice. The finite cutoff and closed enumerator provide a reproducible baseline for higher-order structural questions.
